description: GHCN-Daily station records (PRCP, TMAX, TMIN) for NC stations, one row per station-day; unit-converted in R (precip->mm, temps->deg C). The raw source behind every climate covariate.
citation: Menne, M.J., et al. (2012). Global Historical Climatology Network-Daily (GHCN-Daily). NOAA NCEI.
original_format: .Rds (R serialization; sf long tables, one per element)
use_in_analysis: source for interpolated climate covariates (normals + per-year weather)
known_issues: sparse/irregular station coverage in the coastal plain; -9999 missing sentinel; sf/ALTREP .Rds needs the rdata fallback reader
notes: interim long tables are read by src/peatfire/modeling/climate.py:load_ghcn_stations

description: Long-run climate normals interpolated to the analysis grid: precip_normal (annual PRCP total, mm), tmax_normal / tmin_normal (mean daily TMAX/TMIN, deg C). {element} in {precip_normal, tmax_normal, tmin_normal}.
source: derived from ghcn_daily_nc (NOAA GHCN-Daily) by IDW interpolation
citation: Menne, M.J., et al. (2012). GHCN-Daily. NOAA NCEI.
processing_script: src/peatfire/modeling/climate.py (build_climate_normals + write_climate_normals); driven by notebooks/modeling.ipynb section 1b
use_in_analysis: STATIC matching covariates (stable site climate); registered in covariates.COVARIATES as precip_normal/tmax_normal/tmin_normal
known_issues: IDW smooths and never extrapolates beyond the observed station range; blocky/uncertain where coastal-plain stations are sparse; a surface to match on, not a calibrated climatology
notes: params: baseline=(1991,2020), res_m=300; grid shared cell-for-cell with the fire response and other covariates

description: Per-year (year-specific weather) climate grids: precip (annual PRCP total, mm), tmax / tmin (annual mean daily TMAX/TMIN, deg C), one grid per element per calendar year. {element} in {precip, tmax, tmin}.
source: derived from ghcn_daily_nc (NOAA GHCN-Daily) by IDW interpolation
citation: Menne, M.J., et al. (2012). GHCN-Daily. NOAA NCEI.
access_method: derived (inverse-distance-weighting interpolation of each year's station value)
processing_script: src/peatfire/modeling/climate.py (build_annual_climate + write_annual_climate); driven by notebooks/modeling.ipynb section 1b
use_in_analysis: TEMPORAL covariates for the outcome/DiD stage (e.g. a treated:precip dry-year interaction); registered in covariates.TEMPORAL_COVARIATES as precip/tmax/tmin
known_issues: a year with no station records for an element is skipped (with a warning); same IDW sparsity caveats as the normals
notes: params: years=range(2019,2025), res_m=300; joined per (x,y,year) by build_frame/attach_covariates

description: SSURGO soil map-unit polygons for the NC coastal-plain counties, saved with the relational attribute tables (component, chorizon, muaggatt, mapunit) as GeoPackage layers. The raw source behind every soil covariate.
citation: Soil Survey Staff, USDA-NRCS. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO) Database.
access_method: R: FedData::get_ssurgo (broken download links monkey-patched; see get_ssurgo_fixed)
use_in_analysis: source for the rasterised SSURGO soil covariates
known_issues: FedData's SSURGO download links were broken and are monkey-patched (get_ssurgo_fixed); SSURGO is relational so properties must be aggregated to one value per MUKEY; some county surveys may be unavailable/incomplete
notes: read by src/peatfire/modeling/soil.py (inspect_soil_columns / build_soil_rasters); requires the polygon layer plus the component/chorizon/muaggatt/mapunit tables

description: SSURGO soil properties aggregated per map unit and rasterised to the analysis grid: soil_organic_matter (om_r, % by weight), soil_awc (awc_r, available water capacity), soil_drainage_class (drainagecl, coded classes). {attribute} in {organic_matter, awc, drainage_class}.
source: derived from ssurgo_soil_nc (USDA-NRCS SSURGO) by aggregation + rasterisation
citation: Soil Survey Staff, USDA-NRCS. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO) Database.
access_method: derived (component-percent / horizon-thickness weighted aggregation to MUKEY, then burned to raster)
original_format: derived from GeoPackage polygons + relational tables
use_in_analysis: STATIC matching covariates (soil_organic_matter, soil_awc continuous; soil_drainage_class categorical exact-match key); registered in covariates.COVARIATES
known_issues: map-unit-level values are blocky; continuous properties are depth/component-weighted means of the representative-value columns (om_r/awc_r); drainage class is factorised to integer codes with a printed legend
notes: filenames match the globs registered in covariates.py; an attribute column missing from the export is skipped with a message (run inspect_soil_columns first)

description: Cat's pre-aggregated SSURGO soil database: one row per map-unit polygon with properties already joined on (musym, mukey, muname, wtdepaprjunmin water-table depth Apr-Jun min, numacres, industrial site index, awc). Source behind the soil_site_index + soil_water_table_depth covariates.
source: derived from ssurgo_soil_nc (USDA-NRCS SSURGO) in R
citation: Soil Survey Staff, USDA-NRCS. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO) Database.
access_method: R: FedData::get_ssurgo (patched) + relational join/aggregation to one row per MUKEY polygon
use_in_analysis: source for the soil_site_index + soil_water_table_depth covariates
known_issues: pre-aggregated (one value per map-unit polygon) -- NOT the raw relational export build_soil_rasters reads (that is nc_soil_ssurgo.gpkg); properties sit directly on the polygons so build_soil_database_rasters needs no MUKEY aggregation; industrial (site index) set to 0 where missing in coforprod

description: Extra SSURGO soil properties from Cat's aggregated soil_database rasterised to the analysis grid: soil_site_index (industrial, forest productivity proxy) and soil_water_table_depth (wtdepaprjunmin, April-June minimum, cm). {attribute} in {site_index, water_table_depth}.
source: derived from soil_database_nc (USDA-NRCS SSURGO) by rasterisation
citation: Soil Survey Staff, USDA-NRCS. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO) Database.
access_method: derived (polygon attribute burned to raster; no MUKEY aggregation needed)
use_in_analysis: STATIC matching covariates (soil_site_index, soil_water_table_depth, continuous); registered in covariates.COVARIATES; also in the headline logit adjustment set
known_issues: map-unit-level values are blocky; augments (does not replace) the raw-SSURGO soil_covariates (organic matter/AWC/drainage); water-table depth is most meaningful for drained control sites
notes: filenames match the globs registered in covariates.py (ssurgo_site_index*_nc.tif / ssurgo_water_table_depth*_nc.tif)

description: Self-calibrating Palmer Drought Severity Index (scPDSI) per GHCN station, one row per station-month, computed in R from monthly precip + Hargreaves PET. The raw source behind the per-year PDSI covariate.
source: derived from ghcn_daily_nc (NOAA GHCN-Daily) via SPEI::hargreaves + scPDSI::pdsi
citation: Wells, N., Goddard, S., Hayes, M.J. (2004). A self-calibrating PDSI. J. Climate. / Menne et al. (2012) GHCN-Daily. NOAA NCEI.
use_in_analysis: source for the interpolated per-year scPDSI (pdsi) covariate
known_issues: scPDSI needs a gap-free monthly series per station (panel completed to 2000-2026); stations with little data give unstable indices; sparse coastal-plain coverage; self-calibrating so values are relative to each station period

description: Per-year scPDSI drought grids: pdsi (annual mean of monthly scPDSI; ~0 = normal, negative = drought), one grid per calendar year. Drought analogue of the annual precip/tmax layers.
source: derived from pdsi_ghcn_nc by IDW interpolation
citation: Wells, N., Goddard, S., Hayes, M.J. (2004). A self-calibrating PDSI. J. Climate.
access_method: derived (inverse-distance-weighting interpolation of each year's mean-monthly scPDSI)
processing_script: src/peatfire/modeling/climate.py (build_annual_climate + write_annual_climate); driven by notebooks/modeling.ipynb section 1b
use_in_analysis: TEMPORAL covariate for the outcome/DiD stage (treated:pdsi drought-year interaction); registered in covariates.TEMPORAL_COVARIATES as pdsi
known_issues: no static-normal counterpart (scPDSI normal ~0 everywhere); a year with no station records is skipped; same IDW sparsity caveats as the other annual climate layers
notes: params: years=range(2019,2025), res_m=300; joined per (x,y,year) by build_frame; annual value = mean of that year's monthly scPDSI

description: Combined monthly climate table per GHCN station (totalGDD base-5C growing degree days, monthly mean TMAX/TMIN, growing-season total precip), one row per station-month with station point geometry. Source behind the gdd_normal covariate.
source: derived from ghcn_daily_nc (NOAA GHCN-Daily) in R
citation: Menne, M.J., et al. (2012). GHCN-Daily. NOAA NCEI.
use_in_analysis: source for the interpolated gdd_normal covariate
known_issues: totalGDD is a per-station-year value repeated across the year's 12 month rows; no STATION column (load_ghcn_stations falls back to a per-point id); lowercase year column (pass year_col="year"); sparse coastal-plain station coverage

description: Growing-degree-days normal interpolated to the analysis grid: gdd_normal (mean annual totalGDD, base 5 C growing-season warmth). Static site-warmth matching covariate.
source: derived from clim_monthly_ghcn_nc (NOAA GHCN-Daily) by IDW interpolation
citation: Menne, M.J., et al. (2012). GHCN-Daily. NOAA NCEI.
processing_script: src/peatfire/modeling/climate.py (build_climate_normals with DEFAULT_GDD_ELEMENTS + write_climate_normals); driven by notebooks/modeling.ipynb section 1b
use_in_analysis: STATIC matching covariate (growing-season warmth); registered in covariates.COVARIATES as gdd_normal; also in the headline logit adjustment set
known_issues: same IDW sparsity caveats as the temperature normals; totalGDD is a per-station-year value so the within-year reduce is a mean over the 12 duplicate month rows
notes: params: year_col=year, baseline=(1991,2020), res_m=300; grid shared cell-for-cell with the other covariates

description: LANDFIRE 2024 Existing Vegetation Type (EVT) CONUS, clipped to NC; categorical vegetation/land-cover classes representing terrestrial ecological systems and related EVT classes
citation: LANDFIRE, 2024, Existing Vegetation Type Layer, LANDFIRE 2024, U.S. Department of the Interior, Geological Survey, and U.S. Department of Agriculture. Accessed 8/5/26 at https://doi.org/10.5066/P1XVKXRL.
original_format: GeoTIFF in LANDFIRE CONUS download package
sensor_or_source: LANDFIRE predictive vegetation mapping using field data, Landsat imagery, topography, and biophysical gradient data
use_in_analysis: STATIC categorical matching / adjustment covariate; exact-match key for land-cover class in matching; majority/mode aggregation when aligned to analysis grid
known_issues: Categorical class codes require the LANDFIRE EVT attribute table for interpretation; LANDFIRE warns products are designed for landscape/regional planning and should not be over-interpreted at individual 30m pixels or very small pixel groups; single 2024 snapshot, not an annual time-varying covariate.
notes: Registered in covariates.COVARIATES as land_cover; role=categorical, native_res_m=30, source=LANDFIRE EVT. Use as stable site-characteristic covariate rather than per-year covariate unless doing a sensitivity analysis across LANDFIRE vintages.
